about: The epistola of the formulary “Fifth Sunday after Easter” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Dearly beloved: Be ye doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves. For if any man be a hearer of the word and not a doer, he shall be compared to a man beholding the face of his birth in a glass. He beheld himself and went his way, and presently forgot what manner of man he was. But he that hath looked into the perfect law of liberty and hath continued therein, becoming not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed. If any man think himself religious, not bridling his tongue but deceiving his own heart, this man's religion is vain. Religion clean and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their tribulation, and to keep oneself unspotted from this world.
